data.narrative:
Dispatcher operates in the Defense & Security sector, a space populated by 23 peer companies across public and private markets. The comp universe includes 2 public peers (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private peers, with notable private comparables including Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, Saronic, and Quantum-Systems. The target's specific stage and current valuation remain undisclosed.

The peer-median valuation approach proved inapplicable to this analysis. The Defense & Security sector contains 23 same-sector peers, but filtering by stage alignment (same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables) and valuation-tier similarity yielded fewer than three datapoints—the minimum threshold required for reliable median estimation. Applying an all-sector median would introduce substantial methodological noise given the heterogeneity of Defense & Security subsectors and business models. Consequently, this triangulation method was excluded.

Without a sufficiently granular comparable set meeting stage and tier specificity, quantitative peer-based valuation is not supported by the available data. Further work would require either: (1) obtaining stage and valuation data on the 23 same-sector peers to identify a workable subset, or (2) applying alternative methods such as discounted cash flow or revenue multiples, for which no financial data was provided. The analysis highlights a structural constraint: frontier-tech defense companies operate in a thin, heterogeneous market with limited public comps and sparse disclosure among private peers, limiting traditional triangulation approaches.
